html:
Annam, from the Chinese for "pacified south", was a name used for the Vietnamese lands for more than a thousand years. In 679 the Tang dynasty set up a Protectorate to Pacify the South at what is now Hanoi.

The Vietnamese won independence in 939, after the battle of Bạch Đằng, and called their state Đại Việt. China went on calling its rulers kings of Annam. That is the state shown in the map's 1000 snapshot.

In 1802 Gia Long united the country under the Nguyễn dynasty, with its capital at Huế, and adopted the name Vietnam. That is the 1815 snapshot.

The later snapshots show French Annam. After taking the south as the colony of Cochinchina, France made central Vietnam a protectorate in 1883 and 1884, with the emperor keeping his court at Huế, and ruled the north separately as Tonkin. Both were part of French Indochina. Westerners often called all Vietnamese "Annamese". In 1945 the last emperor, Bảo Đại, gave up his throne to the government of Hồ Chí Minh.
